THE RULES

Make every move count.

8+8→1616 chips × mult
01 / Merge & score

Slide with the arrow keys, WASD, or a swipe. Matching tiles merge once per move. The tiles you make add chips.

02 / Build your mult

Start at 1 mult. Each extra merge in a move adds +2. Consecutive scoring moves build a chain for more mult. A move with no merge breaks it.

03 / Beat the target

You have 24 moves. Reach the target, then bank the round or keep going for up to $10 extra. A locked board costs your overflow bonus. Unused moves do not pay.

04 / Spend between rounds

Buy charms, items and packs. Every shop stocks two random packs, sometimes Large or Deluxe. Large packs offer more choices; Deluxe packs let you take two. Blueprint packs offer deck work, cash, supplies and run upgrades; rare Oddity packs offer riskier edits. Charms stay for the run. The board resets each round; your deck and upgrades stay. Your deck holds 12–22 tiles. Save cash to earn $1 interest per $5, up to $5.

05 / Clear the rubble

Rubble blocks a cell. Merge in its row or column to smash it for 25 chips. It falls more often later in the round. Boss walls cannot be cleared.

06 / Upgrade your tiles

Both tiles’ enhancements activate when they merge; the result keeps one. Each enhancement blueprint or stamp adds its named finish to one deck tile. Workshop jobs copy, convert, or remove tiles. Archive sends a board tile into your deck.

Tile enhancements

Mixed tile reactions

Different finishes can react when they merge. Each pairing fires at most once per move. Both normal effects still fire, and the tile keeps one finish.

OverprintKick + Plus: +40 chips, +2 mult.TemperedPrism + Iron: no shatter this merge; keeps Iron.ShockwaveKick + Iron: break one extra loose rubble for 25 chips.ScratchcardBrass + Odds: 1 in 4 for an extra $3.RefractionPrism + Plus: +2 mult per other enhanced tile in its row or column. Max +6.WildfirePrism + Odds: 1 in 3 to give an adjacent plain tile Odds.

Charms trigger left to right. Additions build the base mult; × effects multiply it. Odd/even charms refer to powers of two: odd is 2, 8, 32…; even is 4, 16, 64…

File a tile

The rest of the board is swept before the next round, so this is the only tile you keep. It pushes out your smallest card once the deck is full, and enhanced cards cap at a third of the deck. Bigger tiles make richer draws — and more dangerous ones.
